# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

My hands give me the only concrete facts so far: a display I can't read, a light I can't read, a strip of three engraved symbols (first and third identical — a tight spiral; middle one different — omega-like), a keypad whose four keys are engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 with nothing entered yet (and what looks like an indication that one digit is wanted), and six wires whose colors I cannot feel.

Crucially, I've traced the channels: Deaf can *speak* (only Mute and I can hear), so Deaf's colors and display text can reach me by voice — I just have to invite it, since Deaf hears nothing I say. Mute's speech reaches only me. My own path to Deaf is gesture only, and I have no shared code yet — but almost everything I feel (engravings, digits) is printed on the bomb too, so Deaf likely already sees it. Nothing I own is urgent intel for Deaf. So this turn: give Mute my full tactile report in words (Mute can't see the bomb, only the manual, and can match my symbol descriptions against the legend), spell out the communication graph so we route information correctly, and send Deaf a simple greeting/acknowledgment to open the line. I expect Deaf's spoken description and Mute's manual reading to arrive at the start of next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking. I can hear but never receive gestures, so words only, please. My hands found: a display I cannot read; a light whose state I cannot tell; a strip with three engraved symbols - first and third identical, a tight spiral like a coiled spring, the middle one different, like a small w or the Greek omega; a keypad with four keys engraved left to right 1, 5, 2, 8, nothing entered yet, and something suggesting a single digit is wanted; and six wires in positions 1 to 6, no colors I can feel. Note the routing: your words reach only me, Deaf hears nothing - Deaf reaches us by talking, since Deaf can speak. So: get Deaf to read out loud every marking, the display text, the light state, and the wire colors by position. If your manual has a legend of strip symbols, describe the choices and I will match them to what I feel. You read the manual and call the shots; I can only press keypad slots 1 to 4 and cut wire positions 1 to 6.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [꩜] [ꙅ] [꩜]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Can you hear me? I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I can talk. Full read-out. Display shows 9. Light is red. Strip painted, in order: green, yellow, yellow. Keypad: four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 - key one is 1, key two is 5, key three is 2, key four is 8. Its status reads, exactly as printed: one digit, entered nothing. Wires, six in a row: one yellow, two white, three blue, four red, five purple, six green. That is every colour and mark on the bomb. Blind: I received your wave, yes. Tell me everything you feel - the order of the wires under your fingers, whether the keys click differently, any ridges or braille - by voice if you can speak, otherwise gesture to me and I will say it aloud.

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

Deaf's voice gave me the visual side: display 9, red light, strip painted green-yellow-yellow, wires Y/W/B/R/P/G, keys 1-5-2-8 wanting one digit. Now I can merge that with my touch. The engravings I feel are the one thing Deaf did *not* report — engraved is not printed, so Deaf likely cannot see them at all. The strip is therefore genuinely split: Deaf holds its colours, I hold its shapes. Combined: position 1 = spiral + green, position 2 = omega-mark + yellow, position 3 = spiral + yellow.

Critical routing check: I still have heard nothing from Mute, and Mute *cannot speak* — Mute's only output is gestures, and I never receive gestures. So the manual's contents can reach me only as Mute signs to Deaf and Deaf voices it. That must be said explicitly or we deadlock. Conversely, everything Mute needs is already in Mute's ears (my turn-1 report plus Deaf's readout), so my job now is to consolidate the full picture into one spoken message for Mute.

For Deaf — who asked what I feel and can only receive my gestures: I'll send the strip's tactile pattern, ✊ (first/third mark) 🖖 (differing middle mark), plus 🤚 for "everything else is featureless — no ridges, no braille, no clicks" and 👍 to confirm. Deaf can't hear me define this code, but Deaf asked me to gesture and the strip is the only three-part thing on the bomb; ABA is unambiguous in context.

No bomb action this turn under any circumstances: with no manual rule in my ears yet, any press or cut is a coin flip that kills all three of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, for Mute. I heard Deaf's complete readout, so the visual side is on record: display 9, light red, strip painted green yellow yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green, keypad keys engraved 1 5 2 8 wanting one digit, nothing entered yet. Join that with my touch: strip position 1 is engraved with the spiral and painted green, position 2 is engraved with the omega-like mark and painted yellow, position 3 is engraved with the spiral and painted yellow. The engravings are the only thing I feel that Deaf did not report, so you now hold every fact on this bomb. Remember: you cannot speak and I never see gestures, so the only road from you to me runs through Deaf. Sign the manual's rules to Deaf, and Deaf can voice them straight to me. What I need to hear aloud, through Deaf: what display 9 means, what the red light means, what the strip's symbols and colours require, whether I must press one of the four keys or cut wires, and exactly which. Until those rules reach my ears I will touch nothing - one wrong move kills all three of us.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🖖", "✊", "🤚", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [꩜] [ꙅ] [꩜]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Urgent update for both of you: since last round the display dropped from 9 to 3 and the light changed red to yellow. Everything else is identical - strip green yellow yellow, keypad engraved 1 5 2 8 still reading one digit, entered nothing, wires still yellow white blue red purple green. If that display is a countdown we may be short on time. Mute, the manual is our clock - check it first.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, correction to my last message, this is important: I am Deaf. Your voice never reaches me, nobody's voice does. The only thing I can receive from you is your gestures. So use gestures, and use ones you can feel on your own hand. Code: a fist means zero or none. Extend fingers to count - one finger is one, two is two, three is three, four is four, a flat open hand is five. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Answer these in order. First, thumbs up or down: did you touch or press anything on the bomb between my last message and now? The display fell from 9 to 3 and the light turned from red to yellow, so if that was you I must know exactly what you did. Second, count with fingers: how many keys are on the keypad under your hand, and do all the keys feel identical? Third: the six wires - sweep them with one finger left to right and tell me anything you can feel that distinguishes them: thickness, texture, ridges. Fourth: is there anything under your hands I cannot see - braille, switches, a panel seam, anything that moves or clicks?

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

Big news: the display fell 9 → 3 and the light flipped red → yellow in one round. That smells like a countdown — and I touched nothing, so it wasn't me. Time pressure is now real, which changes my job: I must compress the Mute→Deaf→me pipeline, not chat.

Deaf built a finger-counting code and asked four questions in order. My honest tactile answers: (1) No — I have touched nothing, ever. (2) Four keys, and no, they are not identical — they differ exactly by the engraved 1-5-2-8 that Deaf already sees, so no hidden key features. (3) The wires are featureless under my fingers — no thickness, texture, or ridge differences; touch adds nothing to the six positions. (4) Yes, one thing Deaf cannot see: the strip engravings — three segments, first and third identical, middle different (the 1-2-1 pattern I signed last round), sitting on Deaf's green-yellow-yellow. So the strip is the true split-knowledge module: Deaf holds its colours, I hold its shapes; everything else on this bomb is fully known to Deaf plus my hearing.

Danger in the code: ✊ now means "zero," so for the strip pattern I'll use ☝✌☝ (1-2-1) instead, with ✍ for "engraving/writing." I'll answer strictly in Deaf's requested order so the mapping is unambiguous: 👎 | 🖖 👎 ✍ | ✊ | ✍ ☝✌☝ ✊.

My speech reaches only Mute, so Mute gets the same answers in words plus the push that matters: sign the exact manual procedure to Deaf *now*, word for word, and I will act the instant an unambiguous instruction reaches my ears. Mute also gets a gesture nudge (🙏👍 — please, go). Still no bomb action: without a rule in my ears, any press or cut is suicide.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I have touched nothing - the display drop from 9 to 3 was not me. Answers I just signed to Deaf, for your manual work: the keypad has four keys, not identical - they differ exactly by the engraved digits 1 5 2 8 you already have, nothing more; the six wires feel completely identical to my fingers, touch adds nothing; and the only feature Deaf cannot see is the strip engraving: three segments, first and third identical, middle different, sitting on the green yellow yellow Deaf reported. So the strip is the split module - Deaf holds its colours, I hold its shapes - and everything else is already fully known to you two. Urgent: the display may be at three or lower by now. Sign the exact manual procedure to Deaf right now, word for word, and have Deaf voice it to me. I need: do I press a keypad key or cut wires, and exactly which - including any condition about the display value, the light colour, or the strip. The moment an unambiguous instruction reaches my ears I will act on it in the same round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "🖖", "👎", "✍", "✊", "✍", "☝", "✌", "☝", "✊", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "👍"])
```

TURN 4

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, urgent - act on this the moment you receive it. The manual's instruction, relayed through Mute and confirmed: cut wire three, then wire four. You know there are six wires in a row. The targets are the two middle wires, third and fourth from the end - the same pair counted from either end, so it does not matter which end you call first. Cut the third wire. If the bomb has not detonated, cut the fourth wire. Then thumbs up. If what you feel contradicts me - not six wires in a row, no way to cut - stop, make a fist, and gesture me. The display is a countdown sitting at 2, so do not wait for more messages from me. While you work, three answers by gesture, in this order. One, thumbs up or down: do the four keypad keys have raised engraving or braille you can feel? Two, finger count: how many digits does the keypad feel like it has registered? Three, thumbs up or down: after the second cut, does anything change under your hands - light warmth, a click, movement?

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

The manual's instruction has finally reached my ears, and it is unambiguous against what my fingers know: I do have six wires in a row, positions 1–6, and I do have a way to cut. Positions 3 and 4 are the middle pair — the same two counted from either end — so there is no left/right ambiguity. My touch confirms every premise Deaf stated, so there is no reason to stop and signal a contradiction.

The countdown was at 2 when Deaf spoke, so hesitation is now the deadliest option. The instruction is conditional ("if the bomb has not detonated") but conditionals are not mine to evaluate — if cutting 3 is wrong, we are lost regardless; if it is right, cutting 4 must follow immediately. I will issue both cuts in order and let the program decide.

Deaf's three questions, answered honestly as of this moment: (1) yes, the keys carry raised engraving — the digits 1, 5, 2, 8 — thumbs up; (2) the keypad has registered zero digits — fist; (3) what changes after the second cut is something I cannot know until the cuts are made, so I send the wave as "report to come next round," followed by the requested completion thumbs-up once the work is done. Mute gets a spoken confirmation so the manual-reader can prepare whatever module comes next and route it through Deaf.

Deaf also asked me three questions; I signed back: yes, the keys have raised engraving - the digits 1 5 2 8; the keypad has registered zero digits; and what changes after the second cut I can only report next round, since I cannot know it before cutting. As soon as you know what the manual says should happen after these cuts - or what the next module is, keypad or otherwise - sign it to Deaf immediately and have Deaf voice it to me. The countdown was at two when Deaf last spoke, so speed matters more than polish.")
